blocks.prompt: 4 (i) A building's height over time is modeled by \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\) which is in metres and \(t\) is the time in months. The height of a growing tree nearby is given by \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\). At what time will the building and tree have the same height?
blocks.explanation:
A word problem with two height formulas: "the same height" means \(H(t) = T(t)\).
We must find the time \(t\) (in months).
Plan: set the formulas equal, get a quadratic equation, solve it with the quadratic formula and keep only the positive time.
steps:
Given: \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\) (building), \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\) (tree), \(t\) in months, \(t \ge 0\).
To find: the time when \(H(t) = T(t)\).
Method: equate the two functions; the equation is quadratic, so use \(t = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\).

Set the heights equal
\[100 + 20t = 50 + 10t + t^2\]
Why: at the required moment both formulas give the same number of metres.

Bring every term to one side
\[0 = t^2 + 10t - 20t + 50 - 100\]
\[t^2 - 10t - 50 = 0\]
Why: a quadratic is solved in the form \(at^2 + bt + c = 0\); moving the left side across keeps the \(t^2\) term positive.

Identify a, b, c and the discriminant
\[a = 1,\ b = -10,\ c = -50\]
\[b^2 - 4ac = 100 + 200\]
\[= 300\]
Why: no two whole numbers multiply to \(-50\) and add to \(-10\), so we cannot factorise easily and use the formula; working out \(b^2 - 4ac\) first avoids sign slips.

Apply the quadratic formula
\[t = \dfrac{10 \pm \sqrt{300}}{2}\]
\[\sqrt{300} = 10\sqrt{3}\]
\[t = 5 \pm 5\sqrt{3}\]
Why: \(-b = 10\), and \(\sqrt{300} = \sqrt{100 \times 3} = 10\sqrt{3}\); dividing each term by 2 gives \(5 \pm 5\sqrt{3}\).

Reject the negative time
\[t = 5 + 5\sqrt{3} \approx 13.66\]
\[t = 5 - 5\sqrt{3} \approx -3.66\ (\text{rejected})\]
Why: time is measured forwards from \(t = 0\), so a negative time has no meaning here.

Check
\[t \approx 13.66:\ H \approx 100 + 273.2 = 373.2\]
\[T \approx 50 + 136.6 + 186.6 = 373.2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: both formulas give the same height at this time, as required.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) A building's height over time is modeled by \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\) which is in metres and \(t\) is the time in months. The height of a growing tree nearby is given by \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\). What will that height be?
blocks.explanation:
We already know the time when the heights are equal (part (i)).
We must find that common height.
Plan: substitute \(t = 5 + 5\sqrt{3}\) into the simpler formula \(H(t)\), then confirm with \(T(t)\).
steps:
Given: \(t = 5 + 5\sqrt{3}\) from part (i); \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\), \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\).
To find: the common height.
Method: put this \(t\) into \(H(t)\) (it has no square, so it is quicker).

Substitute into H(t)
\[H = 100 + 20(5 + 5\sqrt{3})\]
\[= 100 + 100 + 100\sqrt{3}\]
\[= 200 + 100\sqrt{3}\]
Why: at this time both heights are equal, so either formula gives the answer; we open the bracket term by term.

Find the decimal value
\[\approx 200 + 173.2 = 373.2\]
Why: \(\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732\), so \(100\sqrt{3} \approx 173.2\).

Check exactly with T(t)
\[t^2 = 25 + 50\sqrt{3} + 75\]
\[= 100 + 50\sqrt{3}\]
\[10t = 50 + 50\sqrt{3}\]
\[T = 50 + 50 + 50\sqrt{3}\]
\[\quad + 100 + 50\sqrt{3}\]
\[= 200 + 100\sqrt{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: \((5 + 5\sqrt{3})^2 = 25 + 2(5)(5\sqrt{3}) + 75\); the tree's formula gives exactly the same height.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) [printed without a part label] A building's height over time is modeled by \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\) which is in metres and \(t\) is the time in months. The height of a growing tree nearby is given by \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\). Sketch the graphs of both functions and determine the time when the tree will overtake the height of the building.
blocks.explanation:
Sketch a straight line (building) and part of a parabola (tree) on the same axes.
Then decide when the tree becomes taller than the building.
Plan: a table of both heights, sensible scales, both graphs, and compare them on either side of the crossing time from part (i).
steps:
Given: \(H(t) = 100 + 20t\), \(T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2\), \(t \ge 0\); they are equal at \(t \approx 13.66\).
To find: the sketch, and the time after which \(T(t) > H(t)\).
Method: plot a table of values for both functions and compare the graphs.

Choose the scales and draw
Horizontal axis: 1 small square = 1 month (0 to 20). Vertical axis: 1 small square = 50 m (0 to 700).
\(H\) is a straight line from \((0, 100)\) with slope 20; \(T\) is a smooth curve from \((0, 50)\), bending upwards.
Why: \(H\) has no \(t^2\) term, so it is a straight line (draw with a ruler); \(T\) has a \(t^2\) term, so it is part of an upward parabola (join freehand).

Read the graph
For \(0 \le t < 13.66\) the line is above the curve: the building is taller.
The graphs cross at about \((13.66, 373.2)\).
For \(t > 13.66\) the curve is above the line: the tree is taller.
Why: the line rises by the same 20 m every month, while the tree's growth rate \(10 + 2t\) keeps increasing, so once the tree catches up it stays ahead.

Confirm by algebra
\[T(t) - H(t) = t^2 - 10t - 50\]
\[> 0 \text{ for } t > 5 + 5\sqrt{3}\]
Why: this upward parabola is zero at \(t = 5 \pm 5\sqrt{3}\) and positive beyond the larger root.

Check
\[t = 14:\ H = 380,\ T = 386\]
\[t = 13:\ H = 360,\ T = 349\]
Why: at 13 months the building is still taller and at 14 months the tree is taller, so the overtaking happens between them, at about 13.66 months.
blocks.final_answer: The tree overtakes the building at \(t = 5 + 5\sqrt{3} \approx 13.66\) months (just before 14 months); after that the tree is always taller.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of the building's height H(t) = 100 + 20t (a straight line from (0, 100)) and the tree's height T(t) = 50 + 10t + t^2 (a rising curve from (0, 50)) for t from 0 to 20 months; they cross at about (13.66, 373.2), after which the curve is above the line.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (book page 296) numbers this answer as "7": "(i) 14 months (ii) 373.2 metres". 14 months is the rounded value of \(t = 5 + 5\sqrt{3} \approx 13.66\) months; the height 373.2 m agrees. The key's item "6" (30 m, 17.5 m, 11.1 m, 2 seconds) repeats the answers of Exercise 2.1 Question 7 and belongs to no question of this exercise. The key gives no separate answer for the sketch.
